newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish '96 energy consumption up 0.9 pct - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Finnish '96 energy consumption up 0.9 pct - ministry.

text.p: Finnish energy consumption increased 0.9 percent in 1996 to 32.0 million tonnes of oil equivalent, the ministry of trade and industry (KTM) said in its quarterly energy review received on Monday.
Energy imports increased one percent to 21.6 million tonnes oil equivalent although electricity imports fell 56 percent, KTM said. Coal imports increased 26 percent.

The total value of 1996 energy imports was 13.1 billion markka. Of that, 30 percent or 3.9 billion markka worth came from Russia, 21 percent (FIM 2.7 bln) from the United Kingdom and 17 percent from Norway (FIM 2.3 bln), it said.
Total electricity supply was 70.04 terawatt hours (TWh) in 1996 compared to 68.94 the previous year. Imports of electricity fell to 5.38 TWh from 8.50 TWh in 1995, KTM said.

Condensation power supply rose to 13.04 TWh from 8.38 TWh and the nuclear power generated electricity supply increased to 18.66 TWh from 18.13 TWh and district heating output rose to 12.66 TWh from 11.27 TWh, it said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
